findings.title: Exp4 sample size vs degrees of freedom
findings.description: The force of this comes from the control rows: the identical df arithmetic reconciles to the stated N exactly in Experiments 1, 2 and 3, and fails only in Experiment 4, and by 31% of the sample. Innocent explanations that would resolve it and are stated nowhere in the paper: undisclosed exclusions, listwise deletion on the attractiveness measure, or a typo in the reported N. The derivation assumes the two df values come from the models the paper describes -- a 2x2x2 factorial and single-df contrasts against a hanging control -- which is exactly what the Methods say, and is the reading under which the other three experiments reconcile.

findings.title: Pilot selfeval df typo (Pilot study, self-evaluations ANOVA)
findings.description: This is the benign member of the statcheck trio and should be reported as such. The paper describes a one-way ANOVA over three conditions, which has df1 = 2; the printed df1 = 1 is inconsistent both with that design and with the printed p, while df1 = 2 reproduces p = .76 essentially exactly. rivets_anova on the same three groups independently returned `consistent` (achievable F range [0.248, 0.321] contains the reported .27; achievable p range [0.727, 0.782] contains .76). findings.title: Df do not reconcile exp1 exp2 exp3
findings.description: These are individually weak and should be read as a pattern rather than as three separate charges. Ordinary explanations cover each in isolation: a df printed for a model other than the one described, a contrast computed on a pooled error term the text does not name, or plain typos. What makes the set worth recording is that in each experiment the majority of dfs reconcile exactly with the stated N and design and only isolated tests do not -- the same signature as the larger Experiment 4 discrepancy. The Experiment 3 correlations are the cleanest case: all four are printed as r(24), which requires n = 26, while every derivable subgroup size in that experiment is a multiple of 12.

findings.title: Pilot selfeval anova rivets clean (Pilot study, self-evaluations ANOVA)
findings.description: This is the important control on the pilot-study finding above. The SAME three groups, the SAME assumed n of 15 per cell and the SAME tool return a clean result on the self-evaluation outcome while returning highly_suspicious on the mood outcome, so neither the equal-n assumption nor the method is what produces the mood flag. There is no hand-calculation signature either: the reported F does not sit at the truncated point estimate, and 24% of Monte Carlo draws reproduce it.
